title: A Near-Optimal Linear Range for the Erdős Matching Conjecture
summary: The Erdős Matching Conjecture is governed by two competing ways of excluding $s+1$ disjoint edges: one may concentrate all edges on fewer than $k(s+1)$ vertices, or force every edge to meet a fixed $s$-set. We determine a near-optimal range in which the second construction is extremal. For every fixed $k\ge2$, there is $s_0(k)$ such that, whenever $s\ge s_0(k)$ and $n\ge(k+1)s$, every $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ with $ν(\mathcal{F})\le s$ satisfies \[ |\mathcal{F}|\le\binom nk-\binom{n-s}k, \] with equality only for the family of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed $s$-set.
